newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sets 1997 inflation target at 7-8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sets 1997 inflation target at 7-8 percent.

text.p: Vietnam has set a target for annual inflation during 1997 of seven to eight percent, the Communist Party daily Nhan Dan said on Saturday.
"The prime task for pricing management in 1997 is to carry out a study on policies and measures to stabilise prices and to keep the consumer price index at around seven to eight percent," it said.

The General Statistics Office said on Thursday that the consumer price index rose 1.0 percent in December from the previous month, lifting the annual inflation rate to a six-month high of 4.5 percent.
December's month-on-month rise was the biggest since February and eased concern, triggered by a four-month run of falling prices mid-year, that the economy may now be coming off the boil.
Nhan Dan quoted Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai as warning price management officials to be on the lookout for sharp falls in key commodities, as happened last year with rice and sugar.

"And so measures to increase demand to prevent rapid price falls is also one measure for stabilising market prices. The pricing branch should not allow sudden increase or a big fall in market prices," he said.

Nhan Dan said the government pricing committee had awarded Khai a medal for "the cause of the pricing branch". Communist Hanoi embarked on reforms of its command economy 10 years ago, but is still wary of unfettered free market principles.
